s1.explanation: Responds to a single dog-like animal (also meerkats) whose head and much of its body are clearly visible and fill a good part of the frame, such as a dog running, standing or sitting. It fires more when the animal's head is raised or turned to profile (a hound looking up, a wolf howling, a terrier running) than when the face looks straight at the camera. Similar units prefer frontal faces. Activity drops for tight head-only crops, for animals that are small in the scene or shown with people, and for groups of animals.

s2.explanation: The unit responds to a medium-sized, mostly whole furry animal (dogs, wolves, meerkats), especially one with tan or brown fur, seen at mid-distance. It is most active when the head is turned, raised or in profile, as with the howling wolf, the redbone looking up, and the Swiss dog with its head turned. It is weaker on tight face close-ups, straight-on frontal faces, and animals that are small in a cluttered scene or with people. Compared with similar units, it prefers head-raised or profile poses, where the others prefer frontal faces.

s3.explanation: Responds to a dog or dog-like mammal (terriers, hounds, Swiss mountain dogs, spaniels, wolves, meerkats) seen at medium scale, with much of the body visible and the animal dominating the frame. It is strongest when the head is turned in profile or raised upward (a hound gazing up, a wolf howling, a terrier bounding through snow). Compared with similar units, it is weaker on tight frontal face close-ups looking at the camera, and weak when the animal is small in the scene or shares it with a person.

real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to dog-like animals (dogs, wolves, meerkats), most strongly when one animal is shown large in the frame with much of its body visible rather than small in the scene. Head direction, pose, and the presence of people or other animals do not appear to matter.

real_s2.explanation: The unit responds broadly to medium-sized furry mammals such as dogs, wolves and meerkats, somewhat more when much of the body fills the frame. Head pose, motion, vocalizing and setting do not matter.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to dogs and dog-like mammals (terriers, hounds, mountain dogs, spaniels, wolves, meerkats), probably more strongly when the animal is shown large in the frame. The specific claims about head pose, activity and absence of people are not supported.

null_s1.explanation: The unit appears to respond to dog-like animals (dogs, wolves, meerkats) as a category, but none of the proposed within-class refinements (framing/size, head orientation, solitary vs. with people, active pose) explain its activity.

null_s2.explanation: The unit likely responds broadly to medium-sized furry mammals such as dogs, wolves and meerkats. None of the proposed within-class refinements (whole body, head pose, setting, motion) could be confirmed, so beyond that broad category its preference is unclear.

null_s3.explanation: The unit responds to dogs and dog-like mammals (terriers, hounds, mountain dogs, spaniels, wolves, plus meerkats as a looser extension) at the category level. Within those classes it shows no clear preference for head pose, framing, activity, or the absence of people.
